plan.search_objective: Identify authoritative sources reporting West Nile virus cases, deaths, hospitalizations, and surveillance data for California during August 2024 (2024-08-01 to 2024-08-31), covering all target fields: confirmed/probable/suspected/unspecified cases, deaths, hospitalizations, subnational and local locations, and date reported.
plan.search_reasoning: West Nile virus in California is primarily tracked by the California Department of Public Health (CDPH) and county-level health departments, which publish weekly or cumulative WNV surveillance summaries during the transmission season (typically June–October). The CDC ArboNET system also aggregates state-reported WNV data. August is peak WNV season in California, so official agency surveillance pages and weekly reports are the highest-yield sources. The upstream planned queries use overly rigid quoted phrase constructions (e.g., "WNV California August 2024") that may suppress relevant results; this iteration replaces them with more natural, flexible query formulations targeting the specific agencies and data systems known to report California WNV. The 4-query limit per iteration requires prioritizing: (1) CDPH official WNV surveillance page, (2) CDC ArboNET/WNV data, (3) county-level health department reports for high-burden California counties (e.g., Los Angeles, Sacramento, Kern, Fresno), and (4) news/media reports that may cite official figures for August 2024. Literature and structured database queries are deferred to iteration 2 if needed, as peer-reviewed publications for August 2024 events are unlikely to exist yet. Language is English only; no localization needed for California.

decision.decision_reason: Iteration 1 successfully surfaced the westnile.ca.gov Arbobulletin series (the authoritative CDPH weekly WNV surveillance reports) and CDC ArboNET pages. However, critical gaps remain: (1) The specific Arbobulletins covering the August 2024 window (approximately bulletins #30–#35, corresponding to weeks ending in August 2024) have not been individually identified with confirmed publication dates — the retrieved bulletins (#29 and #7) are not confirmed to fall within 2024-08-01 to 2024-08-31. (2) No confirmed deaths, hospitalization counts, or case-classification breakdowns (confirmed vs. probable, neuroinvasive vs. non-neuroinvasive) for August 2024 specifically have been extracted. (3) County-level locality detail for high-burden counties (LA, Sacramento, Kern, Fresno) during August 2024 is absent. (4) The CDC 2024 historical data page (distinct from the current-year 2026 page) has not been located. (5) News articles with dated August 2024 evidence quotes citing specific numeric counts have not been confirmed. A second iteration targeting the specific August 2024 Arbobulletin numbers, the CDC 2024 historical WNV data table, and county-level health department August 2024 reports is warranted to fill these gaps before the iteration limit is reached.
decision.coverage_assessment: Partial. The westnile.ca.gov domain is confirmed as the primary authoritative source and multiple Arbobulletins are present in results, but none are confirmed to cover the August 2024 window specifically. The CDC result returned the 2026 current-year page rather than the 2024 historical data table. County-level and news sources with August 2024 dates and numeric data are not yet confirmed. Deaths, hospitalizations, and case classifications for the target window are not yet evidenced.
decision.source_diversity_assessment: Moderate. Results are dominated by westnile.ca.gov (9 of 32 raw results), which is appropriate given it is the primary authoritative source. CDC is represented (4 results) but the relevant 2024 historical data page was not retrieved. County-level sources are present but not confirmed to contain August 2024 data. News coverage is thin (2 ABC News, 1 LA Times). Illinois DPH results are irrelevant. A second iteration should diversify toward: specific August 2024 Arbobulletin numbers, CDC 2024 historical WNV table, and LA County / Sacramento County health department August 2024 reports.
decision.trustworthiness_assessment: High for westnile.ca.gov (official CDPH WNV surveillance portal) and cdc.gov. The Arbobulletin PDFs are the gold-standard source for California WNV weekly data. County mosquito/vector control district sites (sgvmosquito.org, avmosquito.org, glamosquito.org) are credible secondary sources. News sources (abcnews.com, latimes.com) are acceptable as collection support when citing official figures. YouTube and beaconbio.org are low-trust for numeric data. The dph.illinois.gov results are out-of-scope (wrong state) and should be excluded.
decision.disease_location_time_fit_assessment: Disease fit: Strong — all top results are WNV-specific. Location fit: Strong — California is the primary location signal across results. Time fit: WEAK — this is the critical gap. Arbobulletin #29 and #7 are not confirmed to fall within August 2024. The westnile.ca.gov homepage shows 2026 data. The CDC page returned is for 2026. No result has a confirmed publication date within 2024-08-01 to 2024-08-31. The next iteration must specifically target August 2024 Arbobulletin numbers and the CDC 2024 (not 2026) historical data page.
decision.corroboration_potential_assessment: Good potential. The Arbobulletin series on westnile.ca.gov provides weekly granularity that can be cross-validated against CDC ArboNET 2024 state-level totals. County health department reports can corroborate locality-level data. News articles citing CDPH figures provide dated evidence quotes. The avmosquito.org snippet mentioning "1466 cases of West Nile virus were reported throughout the United States" during the 2024 season is a useful corroboration signal for national context but does not provide California-specific August 2024 data.
